title: Swe entry domain rest idempotency
question: What does it mean for an HTTP method to be idempotent, and which common methods are (and aren't)?
idealAnswer:
Idempotent means making the same request multiple times has the same effect as making it once, no extra side effects from repeating it

GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent by spec: repeating a PUT with the same body results in the same final state, repeating a DELETE on an already-deleted resource just stays deleted

POST is generally NOT idempotent, resubmitting a POST (like creating an order) typically creates a second resource/side effect

A good answer connects this to why it matters practically: idempotency is what makes it safe to blindly retry a request after a timeout or network failure without risking duplicate side effects

Bonus: mentioning idempotency keys as the standard technique to make an inherently non-idempotent operation (like POST-ing a payment) safely retryable
